description: Versioned host-side sensor/module descriptor format (ROADMAP.md:555, v0.5.1 T15). Maps every services/driver_catalog.h driver_id compiled into this firmware image to its connection constraints, default channel template, units, and wiring information, for a host tool (a configurator, a validation script, or a human) to consult before writing a configuration. This data is host-side only and is not executable firmware code -- it must never be treated as authoritative over the firmware's own driver_catalog.c/native_*_source_is_valid() validation, which always has the final say at configuration-apply time. static/tools/test_driver_descriptors_contract.py keeps this file's driverId set in sync with services/driver_catalog.h.

drivers.name: internal_temp
drivers.wiring: RP2350 internal die temperature sensor (ADC channel 4 on RP2350B); no external pins.

drivers.name: adc_voltage
drivers.wiring: RP2350B external ADC inputs ADC0..ADC3 (GPIO40..GPIO43 on RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1, ADC_BASE_PIN=40). ADC4..ADC7 exist on the same peripheral but are not reachable through this channel-driver path -- see the raw-diagnostic-only native_adc_voltage_read_raw() note below.

sourceIndex.note: channel-driver path only; ADC4..ADC7 are reachable only via native_adc_voltage_read_raw(), a raw diagnostic query with no channel/driver_catalog exposure at all (v0.5.1 T12, services/board_diagnostics_service.c)

drivers.name: gpio_input
drivers.wiring: Any RP2350 GPIO not otherwise reserved -- see HARDWARE_MVP.md's frozen GPIO map for RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 reservations before choosing a pin.

sourceFlags.note: pullUp and pullDown are mutually exclusive

drivers.name: gpio_output
drivers.wiring: Any RP2350 GPIO not otherwise reserved -- see HARDWARE_MVP.md's frozen GPIO map for RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 reservations before choosing a pin.

drivers.name: ads8688
drivers.wiring: RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 industrial 8-channel SPI ADC (ADS8688IDBTR), AI0..AI3 wired on this board. Shares the board's single physical SPI bus (SCK/MOSI/MISO) with ad5422 and max22190; has its own dedicated chip-select pin. See docs/datasheets/ADS8688-register-notes.md.

sourceIndex.note: chip supports 8 mux inputs; only AI0..AI3 are physically wired on this board

sourceFlags.note: only these five range codes are implemented -- see the register notes for the full range table

drivers.name: ad5422
drivers.wiring: RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 2x AD5422BREZ analog-output channels (AO0/AO1), daisy-chained on the board's single physical SPI bus; no per-device chip-select, both devices share one LATCH line. See docs/datasheets/AD5422-register-notes.md. self_test's SPI readback may not be electrically observable on real hardware -- see that file's SDO-wiring caveat.

sourceIndex.note: AO0/AO1, this board's two daisy-chained devices

drivers.name: max22190
drivers.wiring: RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 MAX22190ATJ+ industrial digital-input frontend, DI0..DI3 wired on this board (IN1..IN4 on the chip). Shares the board's single physical SPI bus; has its own dedicated chip-select pin. Mode 0 only (24-bit frame, mandatory CRC-5, no daisy chain) -- hardware pin-strapped, not software-selectable. See docs/datasheets/MAX22190-register-notes.md. CRC-5 implementation is unverified against real silicon or a datasheet worked example -- the single largest correctness risk in this driver.

sourceFlags.note: bits above 3 (WBE and reserved) are not settable via source_flags; POR default (0x08, filter bypassed) applies unless overridden

drivers.name: ips2050
drivers.wiring: RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 IPS2050HTR protected high-side digital-output frontend, DO0/DO1. Plain GPIO frontend, no SPI/I2C/UART bus at all -- dedicated DOx_CMD/DOx_FAULT GPIO pins per channel plus a shared DO_ENABLE_REQ line (asserted once, on the first channel to start). See HARDWARE_MVP.md section 3.4.4.

sourceIndex.note: DO0/DO1, a 0-based renumbering of the schematic's 1-based DO1/DO2

sourceFlags.note: no per-channel configuration exists on this board -- polarity and safe-state wiring are fixed in hardware

drivers.name: uic
drivers.wiring: RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 universal protected input channels UIC0..UIC3 (GPIO40..GPIO43), behind a TLV3214PWR comparator frontend. Counter-based modes use RP2350 PIO (uic_pulse_counter.pio, one state machine per active channel); digital-input mode reads the GPIO directly with no PIO involved. Quadrature-encoder mode (ROADMAP.md/HARDWARE_MVP.md 'using channel pairs') is not implemented -- deliberately deferred, see docs/releases/v0.5.1.md T6.

sourceFlags.note: bits above 2 must be 0; mode 4 (quadrature) is not defined

defaultChannelTemplate.note: the correct kind/valueType/unit depend on the selected mode -- see modeChannelTemplates below, not a single fixed default

drivers.name: synthetic
drivers.wiring: None -- no external hardware dependency of any kind. Each channel counts its own read() calls independently, starting from 0 at start(), wrapping modulo 2^32. ROADMAP.md's generic 'synthetic benchmark source'/'loopback... source for host tests' driver, and this project's minimal standalone example driver (ROADMAP.md:590, v0.5.1 T16) -- see drivers/include/drivers/synthetic_driver.h and docs/code/adding-a-driver.md.

sourceIndex.note: eight independent synthetic channels so several can be configured at once without interfering
